subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary external plugins be allowed to invoke plugin-registered Gateway methods, and if so under what authorization and exposure model beyond the current bundled/trusted-official-only runtime path?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose between raw dispatch, allowlisted capabilities, trusted-official gating, or no third-party access.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved plugin Gateway methods or typed capabilities with caller attribution, trust/allowlist policy, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only access
options.body: Treat current main's trusted-official boundary as intentional and ask external plugins to use another documented seam or trusted distribution path.

options.title: Allow generic method dispatch
options.body: Expose a broader method-string caller to external plugins while accepting a larger security and compatibility surface as an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved plugin Gateway methods or typed capabilities with caller attribution, trust/allowlist policy, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the current trusted-only runtime Gateway path and is the strongest routing candidate for this product/security boundary choice.
